answer: Behavioral fingerprint escrow. Each identity registers a jade-hardware token that signs every outbound action with a per-token secret. The escrow records timing, keystroke cadence, and request rhythm, then cross-checks for near-duplicate patterns. When two identities show a hollow match on these signatures, both are frozen pending manual audit. Duplication is thus self-revealing: the attacker must maintain distinct behavioral profiles across every clone or lose all tokens in a shale-slow review. Cost: separate hardware plus sustained profile divergence per identity.
